sections.h2: Where is the Houghton County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The Houghton County Register of Deeds is on the second floor of the courthouse at 401 E. Houghton Avenue, Houghton, MI 49931. The phone number is 906-482-1311. Doors are open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and the office stops taking documents for that day's recording at 3:30 p.m.

According to the county's Register of Deeds page, the office keeps an index and a copy of every recorded document for land inside the county. Deeds, mortgages, miscellaneous filings, plats, surveys and land corner records are all on file. A seller who wants to settle a boundary question before listing can ask for the survey or land corner record on the parcel.

sections.h2: What does it cost to record a deed in Houghton County?
sections.html:
Recording a deed in Houghton County costs $30.00 per document, whatever the page count. The county says that amount already includes the state remonumentation and register of deeds automation fees, so nothing is stacked on top of it at the counter. Make checks out to the Houghton County Register of Deeds.

  • $3.00 extra for each instrument that an assignment or discharge covers beyond the first.
  • $5.00 to certify a warranty deed, covenant deed, land contract or land contract assignment.
  • $1.00 a page for copies of real estate records and $2.00 a page for plat copies.
  • $3.00 per name for a state or federal tax lien certificate search.

Transfer tax is billed apart from all of these fees. The statute behind the $30 figure is MCL 600.2567.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due when a Houghton County house sells?
sections.html:
Two taxes apply to the sale price: the state rate of $3.75 and the county rate of $0.55, each charged for every $500 or fraction of $500. Houghton County has far fewer than 2,000,000 residents, so the 55 cent county rate in MCL 207.504 is the one that applies. The deed has to show the total value on its face, or an affidavit stating the value goes with it.

The state act in MCL 207.526 exempts several transfers:

  • Instruments where the consideration is under $100.
  • Deeds given in foreclosure or in lieu of foreclosure.
  • Court-ordered transfers with no stated price.
  • Conveyances from a person to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild.
  • Land contracts, until legal title passes to the buyer.

The county act's list in MCL 207.505 has no parent to child item, so ask the register of deeds how the county half is treated on a family transfer.

sections.h2: What must a deed look like before Houghton County will record it?
sections.html:
Michigan's recording statute, MCL 565.201, lets a register of deeds refuse paper that misses the formatting rules. Check these before anything goes to the courthouse:

  • Signatures in black or dark blue ink, with each signer's name printed beneath.
  • The grantee's address and the name and business address of whoever drafted the deed.
  • A 2.5 inch blank margin at the top of page one and half an inch on all other sides.
  • Type no smaller than 10 point, on white paper of at least 20 pound weight, between 8.5 by 11 and 8.5 by 14 inches.
  • A single statement on the first line naming the one recordable event the paper shows.
  • Only the last four digits of any Social Security number, and an English translation of any foreign language text.

A correct document is accepted for recording, and the register cannot turn it away over its content.

sections.h2: Can I record or search Houghton County records online?
sections.html:
Yes. The county accepts electronic recording from four vendors: CSC, ePN, Simplifile and Indecomm. Files can arrive at any hour, but staff process them during office hours between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m. The county lists same day recording and fewer lost documents among the benefits, and not every document type can go this route.

For searching, the office points visitors to Tapestry, a pay-per-use site with documents from September 1993 to the present. Searching costs $8.75, viewing is free and printing runs $1.00 a page. Title professionals can subscribe to Laredo for round the clock access. The tract index can also be used in person for $400.00 a month, $20.00 an hour or $5.00 per 15 minutes. A free Property Fraud Alert service emails or calls an owner whenever the exact name entered appears on a newly recorded document.

sections.h2: What is Houghton County like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Houghton County covers 1,502 square miles on the Keweenaw Peninsula, of which 1,009 square miles is land and 33 percent is water. It was set off in 1843, had its boundaries described in 1845 and organized in 1846, and was named for state geologist Douglass Houghton. Keweenaw County was carved from it in 1861 and Baraga County in 1875. The 1910 census counted 88,098 residents during the copper boom, and the 2020 count was 37,361.

The Portage Lift Bridge links Hancock to the city of Houghton, which is the county seat. US 41 and M-26 are the main roads. Michigan Technological University is in the county, and The county has two charter townships, Calumet and Portage. Census Bureau figures for the county show:

  • 37,842 residents in the July 2025 estimate, up 1.3 percent from the 2020 base.
  • 19,308 housing units, with 71.8 percent of households owning.
  • A median owner-occupied value of $159,900 and median gross rent of $840.
  • Median household income of $58,899 and a 15.6 minute average commute.

sections.h2: Who handles taxes and valuations in Houghton County?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's Office is also on the courthouse second floor and answers at 906-482-0560, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. It collects delinquent real estate taxes, certifies property deeds and plats, supplies tax histories and offers partial payment plans. It also posts tax sale and foreclosure information, including a foreclosure timeline.

The Equalization Department covers 16 assessment jurisdictions and reports taxable values to the State Tax Commission each year. Requests go to equalization@houghtoncounty.net or to Attn: Equalization, 401 E Houghton Ave, Houghton MI 49931. Before a closing, ask the Treasurer for the parcel's tax status so the title company can plan for any balance.

faqs.q: How much does Houghton County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The charge is $30.00 per document, regardless of how many pages it has. Add $5.00 if the paper is a warranty deed, covenant deed or land contract that needs certification, and $3.00 for each extra instrument an assignment or discharge covers.

faqs.q: Is the 3:30 p.m. cutoff firm at the Houghton County office?
faqs.a: Yes, the register of deeds sets a daily cutoff of 3:30 p.m. for recording, even though the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. Electronic submissions are accepted at any time but are processed between 8:30 a.m. and 3:30 p.m.

faqs.q: Who pays the Houghton County transfer tax on a sale?
faqs.a: Ask the register of deeds or the title company, because the county page does not assign the payment. The statutes set the amounts at $3.75 state and $0.55 county per $500 of value, and the tax is collected when the deed is presented for recording.

faqs.q: Can I search Houghton County deeds from home?
faqs.a: Yes. Tapestry has documents from September 1993 forward at $8.75 per search with free viewing, and Laredo is a subscription service for regular searchers. For anything earlier than that, ask the office at 906-482-1311.

faqs.q: Where do I ask about unpaid taxes before selling in Houghton County?
faqs.a: Call the Houghton County Treasurer at 906-482-0560 or visit the second floor of the courthouse at 401 E. Houghton Avenue. The office handles delinquent taxes, tax histories and partial payment plans, and keeps tax sale information.
